transcript.text: The extractor fan over my hob has stopped working. Lights come on but the fan just hums when I press the speed buttons, doesn't spin. It's a Bosch chimney hood I think. Is that part of my hob?

No, the extractor fan (chimney hood) is not part of your hob (cooktop). They are two separate appliances:

• The Hob: The flat surface with burners or heating elements where you cook.
• The Extractor Fan/Chimney Hood: The unit mounted above the hob that sucks up smoke, steam, and odors. It has its own motor, fan blades, light bulbs, and controls.

### Why Your Fan Is Humming But Not Spinning

A humming sound without rotation usually indicates one of these issues:

1.  Seized Motor Bearings: The most common cause. Over time, grease and heat can cause the motor bearings to seize or become stiff. The motor tries to start (hence the hum) but can’t turn the fan blades.
2.  Blocked Fan Wheel: Grease buildup on the fan impeller can make it too heavy for the motor to spin.
3.  Failed Start Capacitor: Some motors use a capacitor to help them start. If this fails, the motor may hum but not rotate.
4.  Obstruction: Something physical (like a piece of debris or a bent blade) might be blocking rotation.

### What You Can Try (Safely)

⚠️ Safety First: Turn off the power to the hood at the circuit breaker before attempting any inspection or cleaning.

1.  Check for Obstructions: Remove the grease filters and manually try to spin the fan wheel by hand (if accessible). If it doesn’t spin freely, there’s likely a blockage or seized bearing.
2.  Clean Grease Buildup: Soak metal grease filters in hot soapy water or degreaser. Wipe down the interior of the hood and fan area if possible. Heavy grease can weigh down the fan.
3.  Try Spinning It Manually: With power OFF, try to gently spin the fan blade by hand. If it’s stiff or won’t move at all, the bearings are likely seized.

### Next Steps

• If cleaning frees the fan: Turn the power back on and test it. It may work temporarily but could fail again soon if the bearings are worn.
• If the fan is still seized after cleaning: The motor bearings are likely failed. This usually requires professional repair or replacement of the entire hood unit, as replacing just the motor in a chimney hood can be complex and costly relative to the age/value of the appliance.

### Regarding Your Bosch Hood

Since it’s a Bosch chimney hood:
• Check if it’s under warranty (unlikely if it’s older).
• Contact Bosch Customer Service or an authorized appliance repair technician for diagnosis. They can often order specific replacement parts like motors or capacitors if the unit is still serviceable.

Do not keep pressing the speed buttons repeatedly, as this can overheat and damage the motor further if it’s already seized.

Thanks. I won't go up a ladder to take it apart, so I can't spin the fan by hand. When I left it humming for a minute or so there was a slightly warm smell, and the filters are pretty greasy, I haven't cleaned them in about a year. Is it safe to keep using it?

No, it is not safe to continue using the extractor fan in this condition. Here’s why:

### Risks of Continuing Use

1.  Fire Hazard: Grease buildup on filters and inside the hood is highly flammable. A motor running hot (indicated by the warm smell) near grease can ignite it, creating a serious fire risk.
2.  Motor Damage: The humming sound indicates the motor is struggling against resistance (likely seized bearings or heavy grease). Running a motor under this strain causes overheating, which can:
    • Burn out the windings permanently.
    • Melt internal components.
    • Potentially cause an electrical short circuit.
3.  Electrical Safety: Overheating motors can damage wiring and connections, increasing the risk of electrical faults.

### Immediate Actions

1.  Stop Using It Immediately: Turn off the power to the hood at the circuit breaker if possible, or just stop using the fan controls. Do not press any buttons again.
2.  Do Not Attempt Complex Repairs Yourself: Since you’re uncomfortable going up a ladder and taking it apart, this is wise. Extractor fans involve electrical components and can be tricky to disassemble safely.

### Recommended Next Steps

1.  Clean the Grease Filters: This is the easiest part and something you can do safely without a ladder if they are removable:
    • Turn off power at the breaker.
    • Remove the metal grease filters (they usually slide out or unclip).
    • Soak them in hot soapy water with degreaser, or put them in the dishwasher (if dishwasher-safe).
    • Wipe down the visible interior of the hood if you can reach it safely from below.
2.  Call a Professional: Given the humming, warm smell, and your reluctance to disassemble it:
    • Contact a qualified appliance repair technician or an electrician specializing in kitchen appliances.
    • Describe the symptoms (humming, no spin, warm smell, greasy filters).
    • They can safely inspect, clean internally if needed, diagnose if the motor bearings are seized, and replace the motor or entire unit if necessary.

### Summary

The combination of heavy grease buildup, a humming motor that won’t spin, and a warm smell strongly suggests a failing motor with potential fire risk. Please stop using it immediately and arrange for professional repair after cleaning the accessible filters. This protects your home from fire risk and prevents further damage to the appliance.
